title: Mr. & Mrs. Sambar Kitchen Brings Unapologetically Authentic South Indian Food to Surrey
excerpt: Two Tamil Nadu-trained chefs refuse to water down spice levels or compromise on tradition at their new restaurant — and customers are lining up for it.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Mr. & Mrs. Sambar Kitchen opened in Surrey on January 26, 2026, serving authentic Tamil Nadu cuisine.
  • The Ambur Biryani, made with Seeraga Samba rice, evokes strong emotional responses from customers.
  • Co-founder Vijay has over 20 years of experience in the restaurant industry before opening his own.
  • The restaurant operates daily from 10 AM to 10:30 PM at 12827 76 Ave, Surrey, BC.
Authentic Tamil Nadu Experience
›Opened on January 26, 2026
›Co-founders: Vijay and Balaji
›Focus on traditional spice levels
›Located at 12827 76 Ave, Surrey, BC

Walk into Mr. & Mrs. Sambar Kitchen on 76th Avenue in Surrey and the aroma does the talking before the menu arrives. Steaming idlis, golden dosas crackling on the griddle, simmering curries, and slow-cooked biryani fill the air with the unmistakable scent of a South Indian kitchen operating without shortcuts.

The restaurant, which opened on January 26, 2026, is the shared vision of partners Vijay and Balaji — two chefs whose combined decades of experience in professional kitchens, from Vancouver's Lower Mainland to international cruise ships, have culminated in a single, non-negotiable philosophy: serve South Indian food exactly the way it is meant to be served.

"We don't ask customers how spicy they want their food. If we change the spice level to suit everyone, we lose the authenticity. We want people to experience South Indian food the way we grew up eating it."

— Vijay, co-founder, Mr. & Mrs. Sambar Kitchen

Roots in Tamil Nadu, Built in Canada

> **"We want people to experience South Indian food the way we grew up eating it."

— Vijay, co-founder, Mr."**

Vijay's journey to owning a restaurant began more than 20 years ago, when he arrived in Vancouver as an international student. He worked in restaurants across the region, cooked for celebrities, and spent years quietly building toward a single goal: a restaurant that celebrated the food of his childhood in Tamil Nadu.

He found the right partner in Balaji, a 2007 graduate of hotel management whose career spanned restaurant kitchens and international cruise ships before he moved to Canada in 2018. Balaji's culinary spark came from his uncle, a chef whose passion for cooking inspired him to enter the profession. Together, the pair set out to build something specific — not another generic Indian restaurant, but one that proudly represented the distinct culinary traditions of Tamil Nadu.

![Tamil Nadu. Sambar Kitchen opened in Surrey on January 26, 2026, serving authentic Tamil Nadu cuisine.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f2/Mamallapuram_view.jpg)

The Ambur Biryani That Moved a Customer to Tears

The centrepiece of Mr. & Mrs. Sambar Kitchen's menu is their Ambur Biryani. Unlike the more familiar biryanis made with long-grain basmati rice, the Ambur version uses Seeraga Samba, a short-grain aromatic rice native to Tamil Nadu that absorbs spices deeply and produces a flavour profile unlike anything found in most North American Indian restaurants. The menu also features a Chennai-style biryani, giving diners two distinct regional experiences.

The rest of the menu reads like a tour of South Indian staples: rava dosas, mutton bone soup, uttapams, and an array of curries. But it is the biryani that has drawn the strongest reactions.

Vijay recalls one customer who ordered the mutton Ambur Biryani and became emotional after the first few bites. "He told us he hadn't eaten a biryani this authentic anywhere in North America," Vijay told DARPAN Magazine. "He was almost in tears because it reminded him of home."

The Ambur Biryani Impact
›Uses Seeraga Samba rice instead of basmati
›Evokes emotional reactions from customers
›Offers distinct regional biryani experiences
›Customer described it as the most authentic in North America

A Name with a Story

The restaurant's name has its own origin story. Vijay and Balaji originally planned to call it simply "Sambar Kitchen," a nod to Vijay's mother's signature sambar recipe, which inspired much of the menu. But the name felt too common.

"We added 'Mr.,' and then realized, 'Without Mrs., there is no Mr.,'" Vijay said with a laugh, according to DARPAN. The result is a name that is warm, memorable, and reflects the family values at the heart of the operation.

Hospitality Without Compromise

Authenticity at Mr. & Mrs. Sambar Kitchen extends beyond the plate. Every guest is greeted with water and a smile. Staff are trained to explain unfamiliar dishes and walk diners through regional specialities without condescension. The approach mirrors traditional South Indian hospitality — genuine, unhurried, and personal.

In a market where many Indian restaurants adapt recipes to suit local palates, the decision to maintain traditional spice levels is deliberately bold. The owners bet that the growing South Asian diaspora in Surrey — and adventurous eaters beyond it — would value authenticity over accommodation. So far, that bet appears to be paying off.

Mr. & Mrs. Sambar Kitchen is located at 12827 76 Ave, Suite 109, Surrey, BC, and is open daily from 10 AM to 10:30 PM. Reservations and inquiries can be made at +1 236 592 5863 or through their website at mrandmrssambar.com.
